items.title: The acoustic environment is structured more by place and fine particulate matter more by time across Rhode Island communities
items.summary: Measurements across 144 sites and 531 sessions found that acoustic metrics varied mainly between places and were associated with built-environment features, while fine-particle pollution varied mainly between measurement days with weather. The authors conclude that these exposures should be characterised separately rather than merged into one environmental-quality index.

items.title: Restorative urban soundscapes
items.summary: This review links acoustic scenes and perceptual processing to physiological, cognitive, and subjective restoration. It argues that restorative effects depend on perceived meaning, audiovisual congruence, listener and cultural differences, and measurement choices, and calls for conditional, testable design recommendations rather than generic prescriptions to add natural sounds.

items.title: Normal-incidence acoustic data for perforated plates with stepwise apertures backed by TPMS cores
items.summary: This reusable dataset reports impedance-tube measurements for 32 combinations of stepwise-aperture perforated plates, empty cavities and three triply periodic minimal-surface cores. It includes absorption, reflection, impedance and admittance data from 50 to 1600 Hz, repeated acquisitions, raw instrument exports and printable geometry files.

items.title: Single-particle limit of a topological edge state in a locally resonant band gap
items.summary: A theoretical and numerical study adds a local resonator to an SSH-inspired stiffness dimer. Matching a topological edge state to the resonator-induced attenuation singularity confines the mode to one boundary particle at low frequency; boundary tuning can recover this idealised state after disorder detunes it.
